what_its_for: This combination medicine helps lower high blood pressure (hypertension) and reduces extra fluid buildup (edema) in your body. It contains two water pills (diuretics) that work together: hydrochlorothiazide helps your kidneys remove extra salt and water, while triamterene helps your body hold onto potassium so your levels do not drop too low.
how_to_take: Take this medicine by mouth, with or without food. Taking it with food or milk may help if it upsets your stomach. Try to take it in the morning or early afternoon to avoid having to wake up at night to use the bathroom. Swallow capsules or tablets whole with a full glass of water. Do not crush, chew, or split unless your pharmacist says it is okay.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your condition. A common adult dose is one capsule or tablet once or twice daily. Always follow your doctor's specific instructions and do not change your dose on your own. Never take more than prescribed.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but only if it is still the same day. If it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Never take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store at room temperature between 68°F and 77°F (20°C to 25°C). Keep it away from heat, direct sunlight, and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets. Do not use after the expiration date on the label.
what_to_avoid: Avoid taking potassium supplements, salt substitutes containing potassium, or eating very large amounts of potassium-rich foods (like bananas or oranges) without asking your doctor first, because this medicine already helps keep potassium in your body. Limit alcohol, as it can lower your blood pressure too much and cause dizziness. Avoid standing up too quickly to prevent lightheadedness. Be careful in hot weather or during heavy exercise since you may become dehydrated more easily. Tell your doctor or dentist about this medicine before any procedure.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you notice: muscle weakness, cramps, or irregular heartbeat (signs of high potassium); signs of dehydration like extreme thirst, dry mouth, or decreased urination; dizziness or fainting; swelling of the face, lips, or throat; skin rash or sensitivity to sunlight; signs of kidney problems such as decreased urination or lower back pain; unusual bleeding or bruising; yellowing of the skin or eyes; or if your blood pressure readings are not improving.
when_it_works: You may start to urinate more within the first few hours of taking this medicine. For blood pressure control, you may begin to notice some improvement within a few days, but it can take 2 to 4 weeks to feel the full benefit. Keep taking it every day even if you feel well, because high blood pressure often has no symptoms.
special_populations: Older adults: You may be more sensitive to side effects like dizziness and dehydration, so use extra caution when standing up. Kidney or liver disease: This medicine may not be safe for you; your doctor will need to check your kidney and liver function. Pregnancy and breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, as this medicine may not be safe for your baby. Diabetes: This medicine can affect blood sugar levels, so monitor your blood sugar more closely and report any changes to your doctor.
